name: Special days of the Islamic year
why: Days and nights Muslims mark every year; Laylat al-Qadr is the subject of Surah al-Qadr.

name: Voluntary prayers
why: Prayers beyond the five obligatory ones; the night prayer is urged in 17:79.

name: Surahs named after times of day
why: Dawn, the morning light, the declining day, the night and daybreak each name a surah.

name: The four most beloved words to Allah
why: The Prophet ﷺ said the most beloved words to Allah are these four, in any order (Muslim 2137).

name: Books revealed to prophets
why: Scriptures named in the Quran: the Tawrah to Musa, the Zabur to Dawud, the Injil to Isa and the Quran to Muhammad ﷺ.

name: Compilers of the six major hadith books
why: Authors of the Kutub as-Sittah, the six best-known collections of hadith.

name: Daughters of the Prophet ﷺ
why: The four daughters of the Prophet ﷺ and Khadijah.

name: Surahs that begin with Alif Lam Mim
why: 6 surahs open with the letters Alif Lam Mim, the first of them Al-Baqarah.

name: The five pillars of Islam
why: Islam is built on five, as the Prophet ﷺ said: the testimony of faith, prayer, zakat, fasting Ramadan and Hajj (Bukhari 8).

name: Animals in the stories of the prophets
why: Yunus and the whale, Sulayman's hoopoe (27:20), Salih's she-camel, the crow that taught Adam's son, and the wolf blamed for Yusuf.

name: Mothers of prophets
why: Maryam was the mother of Isa, Hajar of Ismail, Sarah of Ishaq and Aminah of the Prophet ﷺ.

name: Found at the Masjid al-Haram
why: Landmarks around the Kaaba; the Station of Ibrahim is named as a place of prayer in 2:125.

name: The rightly guided caliphs
why: The first four caliphs after the Prophet ﷺ, in the order they led.

name: Names of Hell
why: Names the Quran gives to the Fire; al-Hutamah, the crusher, is described in Surah al-Humazah.

name: Rivers of Paradise
why: Paradise has rivers of water that never spoils, milk whose taste never changes, wine delicious to drink, and purified honey (47:15).

name: Prophets whose fathers were prophets
why: Ismail and Ishaq were sons of Ibrahim, Sulayman of Dawud, Yahya of Zakariyya, and Yusuf of Yaqub.

name: Washed or wiped in wudu
